title: One Leaf, Many Cups: Tea Rituals Across the World
title_zh: 一片叶子，多种杯子：世界各地的茶俗
intro_zh: 本文约569词，介绍了世界各地的茶文化，包括中国、日本、英国、摩洛哥、印度和西藏等地的饮茶方式，适合CET-4阅读练习。

paragraphs.en: Tea is the most consumed drink in the world after water. People drink about two billion cups every day. Yet the way people prepare and enjoy it differs greatly from country to country. In some places, tea is a quick morning drink; in others, it is a slow ritual that brings people together. Behind every cup there is a story of local taste, climate and custom.
paragraphs.zh: 茶是世界上最受欢迎的饮料之一，仅次于水。人们每天大约喝掉二十亿杯茶。然而，不同国家的人准备和享用茶的方式差别很大。在一些地方，茶是早晨匆匆喝下的一杯饮料；在另一些地方，它却是一种让人聚在一起的缓慢仪式。每一杯茶的背后，都藏着当地口味、气候和习俗的故事。

paragraphs.en: China is often called the home of tea. Legend says Emperor Shen Nong discovered it when leaves fell into his boiling water almost 5,000 years ago. In the Tang Dynasty, people began to steep tea leaves in hot water instead of boiling them with other ingredients. Scholars and monks valued tea for keeping the mind calm and alert. Today, Chinese tea culture still includes careful water temperature, small cups and quiet conversation.
paragraphs.zh: 中国常被称为茶的故乡。传说神农皇帝发现茶，是因为几片叶子落进了他正在煮沸的水里，那大约是五千年前的事。到了唐代，人们开始把茶叶浸泡在热水中，而不是和其他原料一起煮。文人和僧侣看重茶，因为它能让头脑保持平静和清醒。今天，中国的茶文化仍然讲究水温、小杯和安静的交谈。

paragraphs.en: In Japan, tea drinking became a formal ceremony. Matcha, a fine green powder, is whisked with hot water in a bowl. Guests enter a small tea room through a low door, which reminds everyone to leave social rank outside. Every movement—how to hold the bowl, when to bow, how to admire the cup—is practiced with care. The aim is not just to drink tea but to enjoy the present moment.
paragraphs.zh: 在日本，饮茶变成了一种正式的仪式。抹茶是一种细腻的绿色粉末，要在碗中用热水搅打。客人要穿过一扇低矮的门进入小茶室，这提醒每个人把社会地位留在门外。每个动作——怎样端碗、何时鞠躬、怎样欣赏茶杯——都要认真练习。目的不只是喝茶，而是享受当下这一刻。

paragraphs.en: Britain is famous for afternoon tea. It began in the 1840s when Anna, the seventh Duchess of Bedford, felt hungry around four o'clock. Dinner was served late, so she asked for tea, bread and butter, and cake in her room. Soon friends joined her, and the habit spread. Afternoon tea became a social event where people shared news and relaxed. Today it is often a treat for visitors, with small sandwiches and scones.
paragraphs.zh: 英国以下午茶闻名。下午茶始于19世纪40年代，当时贝德福德公爵夫人安娜在下午四点左右感到饿了。晚餐开得晚，于是她让人把茶、面包黄油和蛋糕送到房间里。很快朋友们也加入进来，这个习惯便传播开来。下午茶成了一种社交活动，人们在那里分享消息、放松身心。今天，下午茶常常是招待游客的一种享受，配着小三明治和司康饼。

paragraphs.en: Morocco offers a very different picture. Green tea with fresh mint and sugar is poured from a height into small glasses. The tall pour creates a thin foam on top and is seen as a sign of hospitality. Refusing a glass can seem impolite. The drink is sweet and strong, and it is served at almost any time of day—at home, in shops, or with friends. For many Moroccans, making tea is a way to welcome guests and slow down.
paragraphs.zh: 摩洛哥呈现出完全不同的景象。绿茶加上新鲜薄荷和糖，从小玻璃杯上方高高倒入。高高的倒法会在表面形成一层薄薄的泡沫，被视为好客的标志。拒绝一杯茶可能会显得不礼貌。这种饮料又甜又浓，几乎一天中任何时候都能喝到——在家里、在商店里，或和朋友在一起时。对许多摩洛哥人来说，泡茶是欢迎客人和放慢节奏的方式。

paragraphs.en: In India, tea is often made with milk, sugar and spices such as cardamom, ginger and cinnamon. This blend is called masala chai. Vendors boil the mixture on street corners and serve it in small glass cups. The drink is hot, sweet and full of flavor. For millions of workers, a cup of chai is a short break and a chance to talk. It costs little but gives comfort and energy.
paragraphs.zh: 在印度，茶通常和牛奶、糖以及豆蔻、生姜、肉桂等香料一起煮。这种混合物叫做马萨拉茶。小贩在街角煮好这种混合饮料，装在小玻璃杯里出售。这种茶热、甜、风味十足。对数百万工人来说，一杯印度香料茶是短暂的休息，也是聊天的机会。它花费不多，却能带来舒适和能量。

paragraphs.en: Tibet has its own special tea. Butter tea is made by boiling tea leaves, then mixing the liquid with butter and salt in a wooden tube. The result is thick, salty and warming. In the cold, high mountains, this drink provides energy and helps keep the body warm. Families drink it many times a day. Serving butter tea to visitors is a sign of respect and friendship.
paragraphs.zh: 西藏有自己特别的茶。酥油茶是把茶叶煮沸，然后把茶汤和黄油、盐一起放进木筒里搅拌而成。成品浓稠、咸香、暖身。在寒冷的高山上，这种饮料提供能量，帮助身体保暖。人们一天要喝很多次。用酥油茶招待客人，是尊重和友谊的象征。

paragraphs.en: Today tea is changing again. Iced tea, bubble tea and tea bags have made the drink faster and more convenient. Some people worry that old customs will disappear. But tea houses are also opening in new cities, and young people are learning about loose-leaf tea online. Whether it is whisked, poured high, or shaken with milk and sugar, tea still brings people together, one cup at a time.
paragraphs.zh: 今天，茶又在发生变化。冰茶、珍珠奶茶和茶包让这种饮料变得更快、更方便。有些人担心旧习俗会消失。但茶馆也在新的城市里开张，年轻人通过网络了解散叶茶。无论是搅打、高冲，还是加奶加糖摇匀，茶仍然把人们聚在一起，一杯接一杯。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Tea is the most popular drink in the world after water.
Different cultures have developed their own special ways of preparing and enjoying tea.
Britain and Morocco have very similar tea traditions.
Tea drinking is disappearing among young people.
questions.explain: 文章分别介绍了中国、日本、英国、摩洛哥、印度和西藏等地的饮茶方式，主旨是茶文化的多样性。A项只是开头提到的细节；C项与文中英国下午茶和摩洛哥薄荷茶差异很大的描述不符；D项与最后一段年轻人学习散叶茶的内容矛盾。

questions.q: According to the passage, why did afternoon tea begin in Britain?
options: Because workers needed a short break in the afternoon.
Because a duchess felt hungry before dinner and asked for tea and food.
Because tea was cheaper than coffee at that time.
Because doctors advised people to drink tea at four o'clock.
questions.explain: 第四段提到，贝德福德公爵夫人安娜在下午四点左右感到饿了，而晚餐开得晚，于是她要了茶、面包黄油和蛋糕，后来朋友们加入，这个习惯便传播开来。

questions.q: What can we infer about Moroccan mint tea from the passage?
options: It is usually served cold in tall glasses.
It is poured from a height as a way to show welcome.
It is made only with black tea and milk.
It is considered impolite to add sugar.
questions.explain: 第五段说摩洛哥薄荷茶从小玻璃杯上方高高倒入，形成泡沫，被视为好客的标志；拒绝一杯可能不礼貌。A项错误，文中未说冷饮且用的是小玻璃杯；C项错误，茶中有薄荷和糖；D项与文中加糖的描述相反。

questions.q: The word “blend” in paragraph 6 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 第六段中blend指牛奶、糖和豆蔻、生姜、肉桂等香料混合而成的饮料，即马萨拉茶，因此a mixture最接近。ceremony是仪式，custom是习俗，container是容器，均不符合语境。
